Lisa is a co-founder of Kietzee, a service that helps parents find a Kita in Berlin. To send your child to the Kita, you need a Kitagutschein. It’s a voucher for free childcare.

Your child can get a Kitagutschein if they… Live in Berlin Are registered in Berlin Are not old enough to go to elementary school Children get free Kita for up to 9 hours per day. It depends on their age, and on the parents’ situation. Under 1 year old Your child can go to Kita or have a nanny ( Tagesmutter or Kindertagespflege) for 4 to 5 hours per day. This is called half days ( halbtags) childcare. You must prove that you need childcare with a work contract or freelance contracts. Children who live in homeless shelters or collective housing can also get halbtags care. Some Kitas don’t accept children under 1 year old. Over 1 year old Your child can go to Kita for 5 to 9 free hours per day. It depends on your situation: Full-time ( ganztags) If both parents are work or study, your child can go to Kita 7 to 9 hours per day. You must prove that this is necessary. [§ 4 Abs. 2 KitaFöG] Part-time ( teilzeit) By default, your child can go to Kita for 5 to 7 hours per day. Full-time ( ganztags) If both parents are work or study, your child can go to Kita 7 to 9 hours per day. You must prove that this is necessary. [§ 4 Abs. 2 KitaFöG] Part-time ( teilzeit) By default, your child can go to Kita for 5 to 7 hours per day. You can get more Kita time, but you must prove that it’s necessary. If you work situation changes, you can apply for more Kita hours later.
In Germany, childcare is free for everyone. Some Kitas charge extra for meals and activities. The maximum cost is € 100 per month. Cost of childcare in Germany

section: When to apply for a Kitagutschein
text: You must apply 2 to 9 months before your start date. Your child must be at least 8 weeks old. It takes 6 to 8 weeks to get a Kitagutschein.

section: When to apply for a Kitagutschein
title: 2. Mail your documents
text: Mail your application documents to your local Jugendamt. Choose the Jugendamt where you live, not where your child goes to Kita. Send these documents with your application: Application form It must be signed by both parents Proof of identity Copy of passport or Personalausweis For the child and for both parents and copy of your child’s birth certificate Copy of passport or Personalausweis For the child and for both parents For the child and for both parents and copy of your child’s birth certificate Proof that you live in Berlin A Meldebescheinigung. Your child’s name must be on it. If only one parent applies, you also need… Power of attorney ( Vollmacht) If one parent applies for both parents or Negativbescheinigung If you have sole custody of your child. You can get it from the Jugendamt. If you apply for more Kita hours, you also need… Proof of employment An Arbeitgeberbescheinigung, or a letter from your employer that confirms your working hours. It must be less than 1 month old. It must be dated and signed by your employer. You can use this template. or proof of self-employment A Gewerbeschein, documents from the Finanzamt, or a letter from your tax advisor. or proof of studies An enrolment letter from your school. and Elterngeldbescheid If your documents are not in German, get certified translations from Red Tape Translation or Lingoking. You can also deliver the documents in person. When you apply in person, you get a receipt. While you wait for your Kitagutschein, use this receipt to apply for Kitas. You can sometimes email the documents. For example, Jugendamt Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg accepts emails. How to mail a letter

section: When to apply for a Kitagutschein
title: 3. Get your Kitagutschein
text: 6 to 8 weeks later, you will get your Kitagutschein by post or email. It shows when you can send your child to the Kita, and for how many hours.

section: When to apply for a Kitagutschein
title: 4. Find a Kita
text: Your Kitagutschein is valid for any Kita in Berlin. You have 7 months to find a Kita before your Kitagutschein expires. [§ 5 Abs. 2 S. 4 VOKitaFöG, Berlin.de (December 2025), Berlin.de (December 2025)] How to find a Kita in Berlin
